subject.title: feat: raise (or remove) 3-minute no-output watchdog cap on CLI requests

question: Should inherited resumed CLI-backed user runs keep the 180-second no-output guard, move to a higher bounded default, or gain an explicit disable/tuning mode?
rationale: Current main intentionally preserves the 180-second inherited-user guard after fixing configured timeout paths, and changing that default trades off long silent task reliability against wedged-process recovery.

options.title: Raise bounded defaults
options.body: Raise the inherited resume cap to a documented bounded value and add proof that the outer run timeout still terminates truly stuck CLI runs.

options.title: Add explicit disable/tuning mode
options.body: Add a documented opt-in 0/null or equivalent disable mode with schema, docs, and tests for both enabled and disabled watchdog behavior.

options.title: Keep 180-second guard
options.body: Leave the current safety default in place and close or redirect requests to use existing per-backend watchdog overrides.

recommendation.title: Raise bounded defaults
recommendation.body: Raise the inherited resume cap to a documented bounded value and add proof that the outer run timeout still terminates truly stuck CLI runs.

likelyOwner.reason: They recently changed this exact timeout provenance path and explicitly preserved the inherited-user guard, making them the best routed owner for the remaining policy choice.
